surfaceCoverage.scenario: A policy edit permits self-authored or weakly bound role evidence.
Documented isolation or transition guarantees exceed what the implementation enforces.
A quality script omits or bypasses an independent-role verifier.
Status output hides unsupported, stale, or incomplete role state.
A prepared manifest gives Hardener inputs outside its declared attack-surface-only boundary.
Checklist directs a worker to an unbound path or permits a mismatched report.
Binder accepts a report or attestation whose references can be redirected or whose Candidate binding is stale.
Candidate finalization and later role binding observe different revisions.
Verifier accepts forged, replayed, or incomplete role Evidence.
Schema permits identity fields or findings that binder policy does not constrain.
Reviewer report can self-assert independence without a validated attempt.
Attempt transitions or sequence values admit rollback or duplicate authority.
Envelope validation omits a trust, expiry, nonce, or proof binding.
Manifest digest fails to cover a resolved input or access mode.
Ledger replay selects a non-authoritative retry or loses an unsupported declaration.
Declared capabilities claim isolation that the QA bundle does not enforce.
Orientation regression leaves role state misleading or incomplete.
Role checklist regression permits a producer to review its own Candidate.
Finalization race allows role inputs to bind to changed content.
Imported CI identity can be substituted for role attestation.
Contract tests omit a malformed or adversarial role report.
Policy helper has a divergent digest, selection, path, or surface-completeness rule.
Policy regression leaves a known forgery or retry counterexample untested.
A preserved clean trace is accepted without binding its bytes to the frozen Candidate.
Prompt does not require reporting a concrete counterexample for every surface.
QA procedures allow source, environment, or launcher leakage.
Reviewer can infer unavailable evidence or rely on implementer narrative.
Registry maps a role to mutable or mismatched prompt bytes.

scenarios: HIGH: readCandidateTraces catches every parse, path, and digest error and silently omits the trace. A required deterministic gate can therefore be malformed or unreadable while the generated reviewer/hardener inputs still appear valid with an empty deterministicEvidence list. The acceptance requires unavailable affected Evidence to block rather than silently disappear; malformed candidate-bound traces must produce a blocking preparation failure.

LIMITATION: the clarified contracts retract the prior input-scope, opaque-launcher, frozen-revision, lock-takeover, transition, and external-envelope findings. No additional concrete QA read path is established from the authorized materials: optional Host isolation is expressly a disclosed limitation, and internal Host execution is not itself a source-leak finding.
